title: Repository Hygiene Capstone — Putting It All Together
learning_objectives: Execute a complete feature workflow from issue to merged PR using all P01-M03 conventions
Write atomic conventional commits with clear subject lines, bodies where needed, and issue footers
Open a PR using the Helm PR template with a complete, reviewer-friendly description
Review the resulting commit history and articulate what makes it professional
outline: Capstone task: add CONTRIBUTING.md to the Helm repo
Phase 1 — Setup: create issue, create branch using naming conventions
Phase 2 — Commits: make 3-4 atomic conventional commits building CONTRIBUTING.md
Phase 3 — PR: open PR using Helm template, fill all sections, link to issue
Phase 4 — Review: examine git log --oneline, confirm conventions throughout
Phase 5 — Merge: merge PR, confirm issue auto-closes, review final history

helm_context.feature: Complete professional repo hygiene infrastructure for Helm
helm_context.deliverable: CONTRIBUTING.md merged to main via a fully conventional PR with linked issue

criteria: Issue created and linked to the PR
Branch name follows convention (feat/, docs/, etc.)
3-4 atomic conventional commits with correct subjects
At least one commit includes a well-written body
PR description uses Helm template with all sections complete
PR uses Closes #N to auto-close the issue
CONTRIBUTING.md content references commit conventions and PR template
Merged PR auto-closes the issue — confirmed in GitHub UI

resources.title: How to Write a Good CONTRIBUTING.md

professor_constraints: This is the module capstone — learner should feel the workflow click together
Let the learner lead; offer guidance only when they're stuck
The CONTRIBUTING.md content should reference what they built: commit conventions, PR template, issue linking
Celebrate completion — P01-M03 is the foundation for all 27+ remaining phases
